name: BFI Doc Society Production Fund
what: Non-recoupable grants for production and completion of director-led, independent UK non-fiction feature films intended for theatrical release. Runs two strands: Directions (first and second-time directors) and Momentum (more established directors).
amount: Up to £150,000 (non-recoupable); total Doc Society contribution per project capped at £150,000 across all stages
eligibility: Producers apply; UK filmmakers; project must meet at least three of the fund's six aims; two-stage process (Expression of Interest, then full application)
next_window: Rolling: opened 7 May 2026, closes Summer 2028
notes: Application link is inside the guidelines PDF, not on the page. Notable films are from the BFI Doc Society film directory, which covers all its funds, not only this one.

name: BFI Doc Society Development Fund
what: Grants for research and development of director-led UK feature documentaries aimed at theatrical release, covering things like finding contributors, building the story, shooting a teaser and testing creative approaches.
eligibility: Producers apply; UK filmmakers; debut and experienced directors and producers; BFI Diversity Standards must be completed before applying
next_window: Round 2 opens 9 Nov 2026, closes 1pm 21 Dec 2026
notes: Page title wrongly reads 'Production Fund' but content is the Development Fund. Round 1 ran 24 Jun to 5 Aug 2026.

name: BFI Doc Society RAD Fund
what: Small early-development grants for first and second-time UK feature documentary makers, for research, test shoots, treatments, contributor and archive agreements and budgeting.
eligibility: First and second-time feature documentary makers; individuals, teams or UK-registered companies
next_window: Round 2 opens 9 Nov 2026, closes 1pm 21 Dec 2026

name: BFI Doc Society Made of Truth
what: Annual fund for short non-fiction films (live action or animation, 5 to 40 minutes) by early career UK filmmakers; backs up to 13 shorts a year.
eligibility: Early career teams of at least two (producer and director); both UK residents; director must not have had a commercial distribution deal for a non-fiction feature in the last five years
next_window: Opens spring 2027 (once a year)

name: BFI Doc Society Expanded Screen Fund
what: Funds development and production of non-fiction immersive work (VR, AR, MR, 360) for audiences beyond cinemas, such as festivals and exhibition spaces.
eligibility: Producers with a track record delivering immersive work; non-fiction only; must meet at least three of the fund's six aims
next_window: Opens spring 2027 (once a year)

name: Screen Scotland Film Development and Production Fund
what: Development and production funding for feature films and feature documentaries made by filmmakers based in Scotland.
eligibility: Filmmakers based in Scotland; Step 1 via the BFI portal (Diversity Standards are part of eligibility), then Screen Scotland form
next_window: No deadline stated on the page; timescales are in the fund guidance
notes: Amounts and deadlines are in the guidance PDF, which was not read. No email printed; contact via Screen Scotland enquiries page.

name: Screen Scotland Broadcast Content Fund
what: Development (single project or slate) and production funding for broadcast content of all genres, including factual, from Scottish production companies.
eligibility: Eligible Scottish production companies; must show a clear need for public funding
next_window: No deadline stated on the page; timescales are in the fund guidance
notes: Amounts, broadcaster-attachment rules and deadlines are in the guidance PDF, not read. No email printed on page.

name: Ffilm Cymru Feature Film Development
what: Development awards for a single feature film or feature documentary with Welsh talent in a lead role, to get it ready for financing.
amount: Small awards up to £10,000; large awards up to £24,999
eligibility: Writer, writer-director or writer/producer/director teams; at least one lead role Wales born or based; applicant holds the rights
next_window: Deadlines in 2026-27: 2 Jul 2026, 2 Oct 2026, 2 Feb 2027 (midday)
notes: Documentary applicants must also give a breakdown of spend to date and how it was financed. Questions: ihsana@ffilmcymruwales.com.

name: Ffilm Cymru Beacons Short Film Funding
what: Funds development and production of live action, documentary and animated short films (up to 15 minutes) led by Welsh directors.
eligibility: Director born in or based in Wales; team members must not have directed a feature with a commercial distribution deal
next_window: not yet announced
notes: Page shows 'currently closed' alongside a 12 June 2026 deadline; treated as the last deadline. Documentary entrants submit a treatment.

name: Screen Ireland First Stage Documentary Development
what: Development funding (repayable loan) for concept work, teasers, research and story work on a documentary feature or series.
eligibility: Independent production companies registered in the Republic of Ireland with office and staff there; rights access or agreements with director and contributors
next_window: 2027 dates not yet announced (2026 had four deadlines)
notes: All Screen Ireland development funding is a repayable loan. No email printed.

name: Screen Ireland Documentary Production: Feature Film
what: Production loans for feature documentaries originated and led by Irish talent, in English or Irish, with international appeal.
eligibility: Teams of Irish producers, writers and directors; rights owned by the production company; one-hour TV slot docs not supported; ROI registered company
next_window: 2027 dates not yet announced (2026 had four deadlines)
notes: Production funding is a repayable loan. Screen Ireland also has documentary TV series and creative co-production schemes (not checked in detail).

name: IDFA Bertha Fund Classic
what: Grants for creative documentaries by filmmakers from eligible countries in Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe, Latin America, the Caribbean and Oceania, for development or (post-)production.
eligibility: Directors must hold nationality of, and live and work in, an eligible country; for production the main producer must be based there; no series, curriculum films or immersive work
next_window: Entries open late December 2026; no June 2027 round
notes: Not open to UK-based filmmakers. Exact February 2026 deadline not stated on the page.

name: IDFA Bertha Fund Europe (minority co-production)
what: Supports European producers acting as minority co-producers on feature documentaries by directors from eligible Global South and Eastern European countries.
amount: Up to €40,000 per project (project budget max €600,000)
eligibility: Applicant is a minority producer established in a Creative Europe MEDIA country; at least 60 minutes; director from an eligible country; project at rough cut for this call
next_window: Entries open 15 November
notes: Applicant company must be in a Creative Europe MEDIA country. Cannot be combined with Berlinale WCF Europe, TFL Co-production Fund or IFFR HBF+Europe.

name: CPH:FORUM
what: Financing and co-production forum at CPH:DOX where about 30 selected creative documentary projects pitch to co-producers, funders and distributors; several partner prizes are awarded.
amount: 2027 prizes include Eurimages New Lab Award €20,000; Sandbox Films Science Pitch Prize $25,000; Al Jazeera Documentary Channel Co-Production Award €15,000; Rise and Shine Award €3,000
eligibility: Feature-length (52+ min) films or series; priority for projects with producer and some financing attached; open worldwide; 250 DKK submission fee
next_window: Selection notified mid-January 2027; forum runs 16-18 March 2027

name: VdR-Pitching
what: Co-production and financing platform where up to 15 late-development feature documentaries pitch to international industry, with a cash innovation prize.
amount: No grant for selection; one €20,000 Eurimages New Lab Innovation Award (restricted eligibility)
eligibility: Feature projects over 60 minutes in late development, not yet in production; open worldwide; director has made at least one short; CHF 30 (by 2 Nov) or CHF 40 submission fee, CHF 360 participation fee if selected. The €20,000 Eurimages New Lab Innovation Award is narrower: the project must come from an independent production company in a Eurimages member state (or, with no company attached, a director from a member state), be innovative or experimental, aim at international cooperation and not have had Eurimages co-production support.
next_window: Opened 8 Sep 2026; early deadline 2 Nov 2026 (lower fee) has passed; final deadline 15 Dec 2026
notes: Being selected to pitch does not make a project eligible for the Eurimages award; Visions du Réel and Eurimages confirm award eligibility after selection.

name: The Whickers Film & TV Funding Award
what: Annual award for a first-time director's 50+ minute documentary at late development or early production; finalists pitch at Sheffield DocFest.
eligibility: Open worldwide; first 50+ minute documentary as director; executive producer attached; budget cap and limit on other funding in place; English or subtitled
next_window: 2027 round 'launches in a few weeks' per the Whickers homepage (previous round opened 19 Nov 2025)
notes: Apply page is inconsistent: £120,000 headline vs £100,000 instalment schedule; budget cap £500,000 vs £400,000; other-funding cap £350,000 vs £300,000. Confirm against T&Cs.

name: The Whickers Podcast Pitch (audio funding award)
what: Annual funding award for an audio documentary or podcast project, with finalists hosted at Sheffield DocFest.
eligibility: Open to audio producers anywhere in the world at any career stage; programme must be in English; applicants 18+; executive producer or named mentor attached; up to four minutes of taster audio; up to 2 proposals each; must attend the final in person; free to enter
next_window: Opened 5 Nov 2026; closes 12pm (midday) GMT 26 Feb 2027
notes: Audio, not screen. Five finalists get a Sheffield DocFest pass, 3 nights accommodation and travel. Award is paid to the winner's production company, or to an individual sole producer.

name: Creative Europe MEDIA European Co-development
what: Grants for at least two European independent production companies co-developing a single fiction, animation or creative documentary project for cinema, TV or digital release.
amount: Up to €60,000 per partner (€100,000 for series budgeted over €20m), max 70% of costs (total pot for 2027: €12.5m)
eligibility: At least two independent European production companies with a signed co-development agreement, based in Creative Europe MEDIA countries (the UK is not one: it is absent from the EU list of participating non-EU countries).
next_window: Deadline 2 Mar 2027, 17:00 Brussels time
notes: UK companies cannot be beneficiaries; the EU list of non-EU participating countries (V10.0, Jan 2026) does not include the UK.
max_award: €60,000 per partner (€100,000 for series budgeted over €20m)

name: Creative Europe MEDIA European Slate Development
what: Grants for independent European production companies developing a slate of 3 to 5 fiction, animation or creative documentary works.
amount: €30,000 to €100,000 per project; €90,000 to €510,000 per slate (total pot for 2027: about €22.4m)
eligibility: Independent European production companies in Creative Europe MEDIA countries (the UK is not one: it is absent from the EU list of participating non-EU countries).
next_window: Deadline 1 Dec 2026, 17:00 Brussels time
notes: Track record and country rules not on the page read; see call document.

name: Creative Europe MEDIA TV and Online Content (Documentary)
what: Production grants for documentary works for linear and non-linear broadcast, encouraging cross-border cooperation between producers, broadcasters, platforms and sales agents.
amount: Lump sum per project set by total production budget, from €70,000 (budgets up to €500,000) to €2,000,000 (over €20m). Total pot €23.3m for 2027 is shared by animation, documentary and fiction; at least 8% (€1,864,000) is reserved for documentary projects
eligibility: Independent European audiovisual production companies established in, and majority-owned by nationals of, countries fully in the MEDIA strand; strong cooperation between operators from different MEDIA countries; partners from non-MEDIA countries can only be associated partners, not beneficiaries. The UK is not a Creative Europe participating country, so UK companies cannot be beneficiaries.
next_window: Two cut-offs: 10 Feb 2027 and 15 Sep 2027, 17:00 Brussels time
notes: Figures from the 2027 call document (V1.0, 30 Sep 2026). Topic budget subject to final adoption of the EU 2027 budget. Broadcaster involvement rules are in the call document.
max_award: €2,000,000 lump sum (top band, total production budget over €20m)

name: Eurimages Co-production Support
what: Soft loans or subsidies for fiction, animation and documentary feature co-productions between Eurimages member states.
eligibility: Feature of at least 70 minutes; at least two co-producers from different Eurimages member states; minority share at least 20% (bilateral) or 10% (multilateral); at least 50% of the project financing must be confirmed in each co-producing country at the time of application. A UK producer can only take part alongside co-producers from member states.
next_window: Three deadlines a year; check the site for current dates
notes: Official deadlines page still lists only 2024-25 dates and the 2027 dates could not be confirmed on an official page; three deadlines a year. The official pages opened did not list member states, so UK membership status is not stated here. No maximum amount or email stated.

name: Berlinale World Cinema Fund (WCF Classic)
what: Production and post-production support for feature films and creative feature documentaries from eligible regions including Africa, Latin America, the Middle East, and Central and Southeast Asia.
amount: Up to €60,000 per project; €40,000 for post-production
eligibility: Projects from WCF eligible countries; total budget up to €1,400,000; documentaries submit a treatment
next_window: Two submission rounds a year; portal link appears 4-6 weeks before each deadline
notes: Not open to UK/European-only projects; WCF Europe is the route for European co-producers. No email printed.

name: Nordisk Film & TV Fond Top Financing (Documentary)
what: Recoupable top-financing for Nordic documentaries that already have national funding and distribution in at least two Nordic countries.
eligibility: National base funding confirmed; at least 70% financing confirmed; distribution guarantees from the fund's Media Parties; apply at least 12 weeks before locked edit
next_window: No fixed dates; apply any time (at least 12 weeks before locked edit)
notes: No amounts stated; support is recoupable. Nordic productions only.

name: UK Global Screen Fund International Co-production
what: Non-recoupable grants for independent UK producers who are minority partners on international feature film co-productions (including documentary and animation) or TV co-productions (documentary or animation only).
amount: Up to £300,000 (non-recoupable); covers at most 50% of the overall UK financial contribution
eligibility: Independent UK producers with demonstrable production experience; UK partner must be a minority co-producer; at least 60% of overall finance secured (80% for Fast Track), excluding the amount requested and AVEC, plus at least one other UK funding source; TV projects need two broadcasters (minority) or three (majority); requests above 25% of the UK contribution need strong justification
next_window: Round opened 12 noon 29 Sep 2026; closes 12 noon 24 Nov 2026. Next round scheduled to open February 2027
notes: The Fast Track deadline (12 noon 27 Oct 2026) has passed. No email printed on the page.

name: UK Global Screen Fund Slate Development
what: Grants for independent UK production companies developing a slate of projects with international appeal, including feature and TV documentaries.
eligibility: Independent UK production companies with demonstrable production experience; slate of 3 to 5 projects (2 minimum for animation-only slates); TV slates limited to documentary and animation
next_window: Next round scheduled to open July 2027
notes: Page does not say whether the grants are recoupable or give the last round's dates. Max is per slate, not per project.
